notes: Source-grounded selected trade story footnotes. Years 2016–19 ESPN excluded. No model guesses keeper rights for other transactions.

cases.headline: Jacobs changed hands in back-to-back deals
facts: Thommy received Josh Jacobs from Tony on August 30, then sent Jacobs to Birch alongside Lamar Jackson and Mark Andrews on August 31.
Birch's acquired trio recorded 501.68 started points strictly after the trade through Week 14, plus 103.80 in Weeks 15–17.
Birch lost the recorded Week 15 matchup. These starts are not proof the trade won a championship.

cases.headline: Lamb moved to Birch; Pollard moved again
facts: Birch received CeeDee Lamb and Kenny Gainwell from Stew; Stew received Tony Pollard and Jaxon Smith-Njigba.
Lamb produced 73.00 observed starting points in fantasy Weeks 15–17, but Birch lost the Week 15 matchup.
Stew later included Pollard in the November 8 nine-player three-manager trade. That downstream move prevents a simple full-season no-trade comparison.

cases.headline: Three managers, then two first-round keepers
facts: The November 2025 trade sent Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jared Goff and Jordan Addison to Stilly; Ja'Marr Chase to JMid; and A.J. Brown to Thommy.
In 2026, Stilly kept Amon-Ra St. Brown in Round 1 (pick 8), and JMid kept Ja'Marr Chase in Round 1 (pick 4).
JMid subsequently traded Chase to Stilly in the October 7, 2026 transaction. The keeper receipts are factual, not proof of multi-season trade profit.

cases.eyebrow: 2026 · A keeper becomes a trade asset
cases.headline: Chase returns to Stilly
facts: Stilly received Ja'Marr Chase and Devaughn Vele from JMid for Davante Adams, George Kittle and Breece Hall on October 7, 2026.
JMid had kept Chase in the first round of the 2026 draft (overall pick 4) after receiving him in the 2025 three-manager trade.
Only completed weeks strictly after the trade through Week 9 are eligible for the current 2026 post-trade starter metric; Week 10 remains unfinished.
